players.product: Aurora sodium fast-reactor SMR powerhouses for data-center power (1.2 GW Ohio campus for Meta; Aurora-INL 2028 startup)

quarterly_data.signal: Pre-revenue: year-to-date net loss of $81.6 million (loss from operations $124.2 million offset by $44.5 million of net interest and dividend income); year-to-date capital spend of $126.9 million across all three business lines; ended Q2 with cash and marketable securities of $3 billion ($1.6 billion cash, $1.4 billion securities) including $1.9 billion raised through ATM programs in 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: YTD net loss $81.6 million; cash + securities $3 billion; $1.9 billion ATM proceeds in 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Raised 2026 cash-use guidance to bring forward project activity: operating cash use now $120 million-$150 million (prior $80 million-$100 million) on expensed first-of-a-kind Aurora-INL costs and grid-interconnection build-out; PP&E spend now $400 million-$500 million (prior $350 million-$450 million) on accelerated procurement and construction at Aurora-INL plus an opportunistic fuel purchase for isotope projects; spending weighted to the second half.

Aurora-INL (first power plant): DOE approved the preliminary documented safety analysis (PDSA); site mobilization underway with reactor-area excavation near completion; 2028 remains the targeted go-live; management is 'quite confident in having all the fuel we need for that plant to run at full power' at the 75-megawatt operating level via EBR-II recovered material, Centrus HALEU and DOE plutonium; total project cost with Kiewit still being narrowed, to be disclosed later this year.

Aurora Ohio: advancing a planned 1.2 gigawatt clean energy campus in southern Ohio designed around phased deployment of multiple Aurora powerhouses; entered an MOU with Kiewit for engineering, procurement, construction and execution planning of the initial phase; advancing PJM interconnection applications and transmission studies (more than one interconnection opportunity on the PJM docket). Future power projects 'more likely than not' take place in the Ohio campus.

Customer demand described as 'unconstrained': on the power side 'we've already had the Meta payment, we've had the Equinix payment' and those discussions are the most advanced; every execution milestone 'creates more credibility and it does help those conversations'. Data-center heat-and-power collaboration with Vertiv (heat-driven cooling) announced last year.

Fuel supply — the key deployment constraint — is being diversified: Centrus letter of intent for HALEU covering initial core and reload needs for up to five Aurora powerhouses for multiple years with deliveries expected to begin in 2029 (possible Oklo/customer prepayments to fund the Ohio build-out); DOE selected Oklo for advanced negotiations on surplus plutonium (about 20 tons in the tranche) that as blended bridge fuel 'supports up to potentially 2 gigawatts'; Aurora Fuel Fabrication Facility (A3F) equipment now in production for 2027 installation; Advanced Fuel Center recycling facility in Tennessee advancing NRC license readiness.
quarterly_data.figure: Centrus HALEU for up to five Aurora powerhouses from 2029; plutonium bridge fuel up to ~2 GW

quarterly_data.signal: Execution proof point: the Groves isotope reactor in Texas reached first criticality in early August — substantial construction completed in 229 days and criticality a little over 11 months from groundbreaking, which Oklo calls the fastest greenfield-to-criticality for a privately funded full-scale reactor; the same DOE authorization pathway and in-house build/own/operate organization will be applied to Aurora powerhouses. Acquired ARMEC and Creative Engineers to internalize manufacturing and sodium-systems engineering.
quarterly_data.figure: Groves: 229 days construction; criticality in under a year

quarterly_data.signal: AI partnership: collaboration with NVIDIA and Los Alamos National Laboratory (part of DOE's Genesis Mission, in which the INL-led Prometheus project received a $60 million phase two award) to build physics-based AI models and digital twins for fuel validation and reactor design — design workflows that took weeks to months now 'done in less than a day'.

connects_to.relationship: Aurora powerhouse nuclear power supply from Oklo's 1.2 GW Ohio campus

contracts.signal: Execution experience from Aurora-INL with Kiewit 'can now inform the work required to supply Meta power from the Oklo 1.2-gigawatt power campus in Ohio'; Meta has already made a payment to Oklo and those customer discussions are 'a little bit more advanced'.
